download.title: Download Hoard

items.a: Yes. Hoard is open source under the MIT license. Use it, explore the code, report an issue or contribute.

items.q: Where are my accounts and data stored?
items.a: Account sessions, collection indexes and caches are stored on your device. No extra Hoard account is needed.

items.q: How do I get started and update?
items.a: Choose a download for your system, install it and connect a platform account. Your collection syncs automatically. Get future updates in the app settings.

items.q: Where do Explore connections come from?
items.a: Explore finds connections locally from the text in synced works. They are clues for browsing, rather than platform recommendations or an assessment of your interests.

items.q: Does the preview show personal account data?
items.a: The library uses fictional accounts and generated covers. Explore uses a separate sample of public works with identifiers replaced, creator names removed and dates simulated. The preview cannot read collections stored on your device.

privacy.title: Privacy & data
privacy.intro: This notice covers the Hoard desktop application and this website.

sections.title: Data stored by the desktop app
sections.body: Hoard stores account information, synced content indexes, covers and other caches on your device. The system WebView stores login sessions separately for each account. Do not publish databases, credentials or logs containing personal data.

sections.title: Local exploration analysis
sections.body: Explore analyzes synced work text and publication dates on your device without uploading your collection to an AI service. The website uses a separate sample of public works with replaced identifiers, generic creator labels and simulated dates, without account sessions or credentials.

sections.title: Network requests
sections.body: Login, sync and playback connect to the corresponding content platforms. Update checks and downloads connect to GitHub or acceleration services offered by the app. These services process requests and network information under their own policies.

sections.title: This website
sections.body: The current website has no analytics, advertising or account system. Language is selected through the page URL and the theme preference is stored in your browser. The hosting provider and linked services such as GitHub may log requests under their own policies.

sections.title: Removal and cleanup
sections.body: Signing out in the desktop app removes the corresponding local session and associated data through the account removal flow. To remove all application data, exit the app first and consult the project documentation for data locations and backup considerations.

sections.title: Questions
sections.body: Contact the maintainers through GitHub Issues. Remove account details, cookies, tokens and other sensitive information before submitting a report.

exploration.title: A different way to rediscover your collection.
exploration.description: See your synced works as a galaxy. Start with one item, follow its connections, or travel back through publication dates.
exploration.imageAlt: Hoard Explore preview with a galaxy of works, covers and a publication timeline
exploration.caption: Try 300 sample works with replaced identifiers, generic creator labels and simulated dates. Each visit starts differently. Explore is coming in 0.1.9.

items.title: Let one favorite lead to another.
items.body: Open a work to see its details and related content. The view moves gently closer as you follow the connections.

items.title: Return to a moment in time.
items.body: Choose a publication month, adjust the range or play through months. Filtering changes emphasis while keeping the layout in place.

items.title: Organize on your own device.
items.body: Explore analyzes your synced content index locally, without sending your collection to an AI service. Login, sync and playback still connect to each platform.
